result.dimension: in-window travel guard fail-closed behaviour over a long (up to 23 s) window

findings.title: Travel guard consumes at most ONE position payload per sampler poll, so max_travel_m is silently soft when sample_interval_ms approaches the ~1 Hz payload cadence
findings.summary: `_capture_in_window_telemetry` does a single `queue.get_nowait()` per loop iteration (services.py:7773) and then sleeps `sample_interval_ms` (services.py:7788), so the guard's cumulative distance advances at the SAMPLER's cadence, not the position feed's. Both schemas that reach this guard allow `sample_interval_ms` up to 1000 ms (step probe services.py:1031, motion probe services.py:947; services.yaml:949 offers the full 50-1000 range in the UI with no warning) while the measured payload cadence is 0.991 s mean, 0.711 s minimum (75 intervals across the six banked raw runs, zero multi-step advances). At 1000 ms the guard can only ever fall further behind — it has no catch-up path — and every backlogged payload is ~0.22-0.31 m of real travel the guard never counts. Nothing gates the pairing, and the effect scales linearly with window length, so the new 23 s ceiling makes it ~1.5x worse than the longest window ever executed.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator runs baseline 3000 / step 15000 / settle 5000 (23 s, now schema-legal) at linear 400 with `sample_interval_ms: 1000` — a plausible choice to keep a 23 s capture from producing ~230 samples — and `max_travel_m: 4.5`. `max_samples = ceil(23000/1000)+1 = 24`, so the sampler performs ~23 dequeues in 23 s. Position payloads arrive at the measured 0.711-1.316 s spread: on a run of fast intervals ~32 payloads are published, of which only ~23 are consumed. The guard's cumulative sum reaches only ~23/32 of true travel, so it does not cross 4.5 m until the mower has actually driven ~6.5-6.9 m — 2.0-2.4 m past the exposure bound the run was authorized against, and far past the 0.50 m overshoot allowance used for corridor sizing. Even in the typical case the backlog random-walks to 1-3 payloads (0.3-0.9 m of uncounted travel) by window end, because consumption is hard-capped at one per poll. Containment itself survives only because beta98's new `clock_bound` sizes the corridor from speed x window; the guard's own stated bound does not.

findings.title: Travel guard re-reads its sequence baseline from handle.latest_position_sample AFTER the movement command is dispatched, discarding the origin sample it already holds
findings.summary: The race is REAL in the current tree, but its probability at the measured cadence is far lower than a MEDIUM. `_step_response_probe_impl` obtains `origin_sample` from `_wait_for_position_subscription_ready` and records its sequence at services.py:10341, then never passes it to the sampler; `_capture_in_window_telemetry` instead re-derives `guard_state["sequence"]` from `handle.latest_position_sample` at services.py:7752, at task start. Confirmed against pinned pymammotion: `_publish_position_sample` (device/handle.py:669-695) increments `_position_sequence`, assigns `_latest_position_sample`, and offers the same sample to every open stream in one synchronous block — so a payload published in the gap advances the baseline AND sits in the queue, and the first `_apply_travel_guard` call then sees `sequence != guard_state["sequence"] + 1` (services.py:7654) and trips `position_sequence_gap`. It fails CLOSED (travel_abort set, mandatory stop delivered), so this costs a supervised run, not safety. `_continuous_decision_loop` already does it correctly by taking `opening_sequence` as a parameter.
findings.failure_scenario: The exposed gap is exactly the dispatch latency: in the six banked runs `command_result.duration_ms` was 73.2 / 115.9 / 186.1 / 185.9 / 190.0 / 258.9 ms and the first sample followed within 0.5 ms, so the window is 73-259 ms starting immediately after the origin payload was consumed. A trip needs a payload to land inside that window, i.e. an inter-payload interval below ~0.26-0.35 s; the shortest of 75 measured intervals is 0.711 s (2.4x longer) and no multi-step sequence advance was ever observed. So: real defect, empirical probability 0/75 intervals and 0/6 runs, and it would present as an instant `position_sequence_gap` abort at t~0.1 s on a perfectly healthy feed — the same misleading signature that cost the 2026-08-30 linear-300 speed check.

findings.title: Feed-stale clock is seeded from task start rather than the origin sample's receipt time, extending the first stale-abort deadline past _PROBE_FEED_STALE_ABORT_MS
findings.summary: `guard_state["last_receipt_at"] = time.monotonic()` at services.py:7754 is taken when the sampler task begins, which is after the movement command was dispatched. The origin sample's `received_at_monotonic` (already available on the `origin_sample` the caller holds) is earlier by the dispatch latency plus the readiness consumption/pipeline latency. Every subsequent update uses the true receipt time (services.py:7657), so this affects only the first interval — but during that interval the guard's silence budget is `_PROBE_FEED_STALE_ABORT_MS` plus that offset rather than 2000 ms.
findings.failure_scenario: The report subscription is live at readiness but the feed dies the instant the movement command goes out (the documented burst-then-stall-after-reconnect pattern, n=2). The last real payload was received at T; the sampler seeds `last_receipt_at` at T + 73-259 ms (measured dispatch latencies). `feed_stale` therefore trips at T + ~2.07-2.26 s instead of T + 2.0 s, so the mower drives up to ~0.08 m further blind at linear 400 (0.295 m/s) than the constant advertises before the mandatory stop begins. Bounded and minor, but it is a fail-late on the one bound that governs driving with no position evidence at all.

result.notes:
(a) PHANTOM TRAVEL FROM RTK NOISE — CLEAN, quantified. The guard does sum per-sample |chord| (services.py:7666-7670), so noise is rectified rather than averaged, but the magnitude is negligible. Measured from docs/raw-samples/ (all six banked runs): fitting the straight baseline phase of each run gives perpendicular position residual sigma 0.0003-0.0039 m and along-track residual sigma 0.0016-0.0145 m — i.e. sub-centimetre WHILE MOVING, consistent with the project's registered sigma = 0.0031 m; the "2-4 cm" figure is the pulsed/stationary artifact. Per-step chords are 0.216-0.318 m with 1.6-4% scatter. Rectification bias per step is ~sigma_diff^2/(2d): at sigma = 0.0035 m that is ~42 um, so ~0.9 mm over the ~22 chords of a 23 s window — 0.02% of the 4.5 m budget. Even under the pessimistic 3-4 cm assumption it is 3-6 mm/step, ~0.07-0.13 m over 23 s (1.5-2.9%). A false trip is impossible on noise alone: reaching 4.5 m of phantom travel from a standing start would need ~1000 samples, and the guard only trips when the sum crosses the bound, which real travel dominates. Cross-check on the real runs: chord-sum vs net displacement is 2.778 vs 2.688 (run1), 3.983 vs 3.391 (run2repeat) — the excess is genuine path curvature, not noise, and matches the published cumulative_travel_m to within a millimetre. Discrete RTK jumps (e.g. the recorded 13.9 cm Float excursion) do not accumulate either: `valid_for_motion` is checked at services.py:7663 and a non-Fix sample trips `position_unavailable` rather than adding a phantom chord. Chord-vs-arc under-count on the curved step is ~0.2% at ~12 deg/s and ~1 Hz — negligible in the opposite direction.

Other fail-closed properties verified sound over a 23 s window: `max_samples = ceil(duration/interval)+1` (7714) cannot end the sampler before the deadline, because each iteration sleeps a full interval; both helper tasks set travel_abort on death (10387-10394); a guard trip breaks the loop and sets travel_abort before the mandatory stop; epoch change, stream `dropped_samples` change, invalid position and stale receipt all trip; `max_travel_m` has a schema minimum of 0.10 so the guard can never be disabled; the refresh window and the sampler share `window_started` and end together.

result.reasoning:
The claim's mechanism (one queue.get_nowait() per sampler poll, services.py:7771-7773) is real, but its consequence is refuted by the age check three lines below the dequeue. _apply_travel_guard computes age_ms = now - position_sample.received_at_monotonic and trips "feed_stale" at _PROBE_FEED_STALE_ABORT_MS = 2000.0 (services.py:7657-7661, 899). received_at_monotonic is stamped by the PRODUCER at frame receipt (pymammotion/device/handle.py:683), so it measures end-to-end lag including any consumer backlog; the caller sets travel_abort and breaks on a trip (services.py:7779-7781), forcing the mandatory stop. Backlog is therefore hard-capped at ~2 s of payloads.

I executed the real shipped _apply_travel_guard against the claim's exact scenario (consumer 1000 ms, producer at the fast end of the measured range 0.711 s, 0.295 m/s, max_travel_m 4.5): it trips feed_stale at poll 7 (t=7.0 s, lag 2.02 s, counted 1.049 m vs true 2.065 m). The run aborts loudly at ~2.1 m of travel and never approaches 4.5 m, let alone the claimed 6.5-6.9 m. That claimed overrun needs a ~7 s / 8-payload backlog, roughly 3.5x past the abort threshold, which the code cannot reach.

The typical-case claim is also overstated: at the measured 0.991 s mean cadence against a 1000 ms sampler, lag drifts ~0.009 s/s, i.e. ~0.21 s over a 23 s window ≈ 0.06 m under-count, not 0.3-0.9 m; no random walk to a multi-payload backlog is possible because any excursion is capped at 2 s.

Additional context: the step probe's sample_interval_ms defaults to 100 ms (services.py:1031), 10x oversampled against ~1 Hz payloads, so the pairing requires deliberate operator misconfiguration. The residual worst case (a legitimate max_travel_reached trip taken while lagging just under 2 s) is <= 0.59 m of uncounted travel at linear 400 -- the same order as the long-documented ~1 Hz cache-lag overshoot the 0.50 m corridor allowance exists for, and dominated in any case by beta98's clock_bound, which sizes the corridor from speed x window and does not consult the guard. The guard fails closed with a named reason rather than being silently soft.

result.dimension: Downstream machinery assuming a window shorter than 23 s (timeouts, buffers, leases, watchdogs, accumulators)

findings.title: step_path_contained's clock bound omits the 0.50 m stop overshoot, and the clock branch only binds above ~16.7 s
findings.summary: `required = round(max(max_travel_m + stop_overshoot_m, clock_bound_m), 6)` adds the stop/guard overshoot to the travel-budget branch but not to the wall-clock branch, so in the exact failure mode the clock bound exists for (guard no-ops, window runs to the clock, then the mandatory stop is issued) the certified corridor is short by the full post-stop creep.
findings.failure_scenario: linear_speed 400, baseline 3000 / step 15000 / settle 5000 = 23000 ms, max_travel_m 4.5. clock_bound_m = 7.5e-04 * 400 * 23.0 = 6.90 m; travel_budget_bound_m = 5.00 m; required_radius_m = 6.90 m (pinned by tests/components/mammotion/test_step_response_probe.py:999-1001). The operator freezes a corridor with exactly 6.90 m of clearance and the gate passes. The documented latched-position mode then occurs (2026-08-28: 21 bit-identical x/y samples with advancing sequence and fresh receipt timestamps across 0.4375 m of real travel) -- `feed_stale` never fires because payloads keep arriving, `cumulative_distance_m` stays ~0, `max_travel_reached` never trips, and the window runs the full 23 s to ~6.90 m. `_manual_velocity_stop_attempt` then fires and the mower creeps a further 0.4544 m (measured, attempt 5, docs/evidence-phase2-steering-attempt5-20260828.json) -- ~7.35 m of real extent against a 6.90 m corridor, i.e. 0.45 m outside a boundary the gate certified. This is new at 23 s: with max_travel_m 4.5 at linear 400 the clock branch first beats the travel branch at 5.00/0.30 = 16.67 s, so every window ever executed (longest 15.2 s) took the travel branch, which does carry the overshoot. The identical omission exists in `corridor_must_cover_m` at services.py:7945-7953.

findings.title: Nothing renews the device report subscription for the life of the lease; a 23 s window rides one RPT_START for ~27 s un-renewed
findings.summary: `stream_duration_ms = max(10_000, total_ms + 5_000)` is sent once as the ReportInfoCfg `timeout` and is never refreshed. Both loops that would send RPT_KEEP are gated off by the lease, and pymammotion's own continuous-stream path never configures a timeout above 10_000 ms precisely because it renews every 8 s -- its constant is documented as 'must stay below the device 10 s timeout'.
findings.failure_scenario: A real 23000 ms run sends `request_reports(count=0, timeout=28000)` (coordinator.py:1761-1763 -> pymammotion handle.request_reports -> request_iot_sys, no `period`/renewal). For the rest of the run nothing renews it: `ble_polling_loop` does `if handle.exclusive_report_subscription_active is True: await asyncio.sleep(0.1); continue` (pymammotion/device/ble_loop.py:174-176), so its RPT_KEEP branch at ble_loop.py:221 is unreachable; mqtt_loop.py:89 has the same guard; and `handle.start_report_stream` early-returns to a one-shot because a manually driven mower is not `_DeviceMode.ACTIVE`. So the only renewal sites in the library are both dead during the probe. The subscription must therefore survive queue-settle + up to `_STEP_RESPONSE_READINESS_TIMEOUT_S` 3.5 s + 23 s window + stop ~= 27 s on a single configured lifetime, against the 10_000 ms `_BLE_STREAM_RENEW_INTERVAL`/`_KEEP_ALIVE_BLE_INTERVAL` comments assert as the device's own window (ble_loop.py:39-41). The longest un-renewed subscription ever demonstrated is the 2026-09-01 run at ~18 s elapsed on a 20200 ms configured timeout. If the device caps or ignores `timeout` beyond its own ceiling, position payloads stop mid-settle, `_apply_travel_guard` trips `feed_stale` after `_PROBE_FEED_STALE_ABORT_MS` = 2000 ms (services.py:7646-7650), the window aborts and `_step_response_completion_reason` reports the generic "travel_guard_tripped" -- a fail-closed but fully censored supervised run, and the operator sees the same reason string a real distance trip produces.

findings.title: services.yaml still documents the containment rule as max_travel_m + 0.50 m, which is not what the gate requires above ~16.7 s
findings.summary: The service description tells the operator the corridor 'must clear max_travel_m plus 0.50 m of stopping overshoot in EVERY direction'. beta98 changed `step_path_contained` to `max(max_travel_m + 0.50, clock_bound)`, and the clock bound is the binding one for every long window, but the prose was not updated.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator planning a 23 s run at max_travel_m 4.5 reads services.yaml, scans and freezes a corridor with 5.00 m of clearance (max_travel_m + 0.50), walks the yard, places the mower, arms the gate -- and the call is refused with `step_path_contained` because the gate wants 6.90 m. Fail-closed, so not unsafe, but it burns a supervised trip and a corridor scan on a requirement the operator-facing documentation does not state. The in-code comment at services.py:9682-9684 is also stale for the same reason: it still quotes 'the clock bound is 6.44 m against a 5.00 m requirement -- a ~1.4 m breach', computed at the old `_PROBE_SPEED_PER_LINEAR_UNIT_MS` 7.0e-04; at the shipped 7.5e-04 it is 6.90 m and a ~1.9 m breach.

findings.title: travel_projection emits a caveat that linear 300's sustained speed has never been measured, contradicting the constant it is describing
findings.summary: The `caveat` string returned in every response says the linear-300 typical speed is EXTRAPOLATED and never measured sustained, while `_PROBE_SPEED_PER_LINEAR_UNIT_MS`'s own comment (services.py:907) records a direct Phase A measurement of 0.223 m/s at 300 -- which is exactly the value `_STEP_RESPONSE_TYPICAL_SPEED_BY_LINEAR[300]` now holds. The caveat is also emitted unconditionally, including on linear-400 runs where it is irrelevant.
findings.failure_scenario: Linear 300 exists specifically so a long step phase fits the travel budget -- it is the configuration that makes a 20-23 s window viable at all. An operator sizing a 23 s Phase B run reads `travel_projection.typical_travel_m` = 5.13 m and the attached caveat telling them the number is an unmeasured extrapolation, and discounts it (or picks linear 400 instead, where the clock bound jumps from 5.18 m to 6.90 m and the corridor requirement grows by 1.7 m). The caveat was true when the 300 entry was 0.16 m/s scaled from a 4 s ramp-inclusive sample; the 2026-09-03 correction that replaced it with a measured 0.223 m/s left the string behind.

result.notes:
Scope of the sweep, so a later session knows what was actually checked rather than assumed.

CLEAN (verified, not assumed):
- Sampler: `_capture_in_window_telemetry` scales -- `max_samples = ceil(23000/100)+1 = 231`, deadline is absolute from `window_started`, no fixed buffer (services.py:7711-7714).
- Refresh loop: `_continuous_refresh_window` `max_refreshes = 23.0/0.2 = 115`, fixed-cadence-from-start with an independent `remaining <= 0` deadline break, so slow writes cannot overrun (services.py:8852-8866).
- Phase scheduler: `_hold_until` sleeps in 0.05 s slices against absolute `window_started + elapsed_ms/1000`; ~460 iterations, no drift, no cap (services.py:9751-9758).
- Position stream: `_SAFETY_POSITION_STREAM_MAXSIZE = 64` against ~23 arrivals at ~0.991 s VIO cadence over 23 s, drained once per 100 ms tick -- ~3x headroom, and `dropped_samples` (the `position_sequence_gap` trip) cannot fire. The maxsize=1 class of bug is not present at either the wrapper (services.py:10503) or the shared sampler (services.py:7730).
- Report lease: `exclusive_report_subscription` has no timer and no expiry; released only by the context manager (pymammotion/device/handle.py:758-799).
- Command queue: `_COMMAND_TTL = 120.0` s, ~5x the whole window; `Priority.NORMAL` motion items are exempt from nothing that fires inside 23 s (pymammotion/messaging/command_queue.py:46, 240-251).
- Background interference: both `ble_polling_loop` (ble_loop.py:174) and the MQTT loop (mqtt_loop.py:89) skip entirely while the lease is held; `_BLE_STREAM_STALE_THRESHOLD = 15.0` s therefore cannot fire mid-window despite sitting right inside the newly permitted range. `ble_activity_loop`'s 5 s GATT heartbeat is independent of the lease and keeps the link up.
- Map saga: the probe is registered through `_wrap_exclusive_manual_motion` (services.py:21108-21118), so `manual_motion_owner` is set and `_should_start_map_sync` / `_raise_if_manual_motion_in_progress` block a mid-window saga (coordinator.py:1127, 1149).
- HA service layer: homeassistant 2026.7.1 has no `SERVICE_CALL_LIMIT` (removed upstream); `supports_response=SupportsResponse.ONLY` calls block without a core-side deadline. No in-tree caller invokes this service -- `grep -rn step_response_probe scripts/ www/` is empty -- so none of the 20-45 s `urlopen` timeouts in scripts/ apply. A caller added later would need > ~30 s.
- Per-write timeouts (`_BLE_MOTION_WRITE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `_BLE_MOTION_QUEUE_START_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, services.py:7391/7417) are per-command and window-length independent.
- Accumulators: 231 samples + ~116 refresh completion floats + course_series; response payload is ~100 KB order, no unbounded growth.
- Schema sum: 5000 + 15000 + 6000 = 26000 exceeds `_STEP_RESPONSE_MAX_TOTAL_MS`, caught by `step_window_too_long` (services.py:10165).

The fixed 5000 ms headroom in `stream_duration_ms` is NOT window-length dependent (readiness consumes the same up-to-3.5 s at 15 s as at 23 s), so it is folded into finding 2 rather than reported separately.

result.reasoning:
REFUTED — the claim's factual reading of the plumbing is accurate, but its load-bearing premise (a device-imposed ~10 s subscription ceiling) is false, and the repo's own hardware evidence disproves it.

1. The "10 s device timeout" is pymammotion's OWN configured value, not a measured device cap. `_enqueue_ble_stream_command` (pymammotion/device/handle.py:1698-1721) hardcodes `timeout=10_000` on every RPT_START/RPT_KEEP it sends, so `_BLE_STREAM_RENEW_INTERVAL = 8.0` (ble_loop.py:41) sits below a lifetime that path chose for itself. `_send_one_shot_report` hardcodes the same 10_000. By contrast `handle.request_reports(count, timeout)` (handle.py:1684) takes `timeout` as a caller parameter precisely so a caller can configure a longer subscription — which is what `coordinator.async_start_continuous_reports` (coordinator.py:1744-1764) does, and its docstring already states the design: "The device-side `timeout` bounds the subscription so it expires on its own." The renew comment is evidence about pymammotion's cadence choice, not about a firmware ceiling.

2. Direct hardware counter-evidence, already banked in this repo. Two real step-probe runs configured `stream_duration_ms = 20000` (total_ms 15000 + 5000) and each rode ONE un-renewed RPT_START:
   - docs/raw-samples/raw-route1-run2repeat-plus180-step7000-20260901.json: `position_sequence` advanced 473→487, one payload per sample at 186/1099/2111/3024/4340/5051/6165/6974/7989/9012/10034/11149/11973/12998/14025 ms — a uniform ~1 Hz with the largest gap 1.32 s, and NO discontinuity at or after 10 s. Measured from `report_stream.subscription_command_flushed_at_monotonic`, the last report arrived **14.70 s after the RPT_START flush**. `reason: window_complete`, `motion_refresh.aborted_early: False`.
   - docs/raw-samples/raw-route1-stepext-plus120-step7000-20260830.json: sequence 116→130, same uniform cadence to 14.21 ms-elapsed, last report **14.56 s after flush**, `window_complete`.
   If the device silently capped or ignored `timeout` beyond 10_000 ms, both runs would have gone dark around 10 s and tripped `feed_stale` (2000 ms) by ~12 s. Neither did — 5 s past the hypothesised ceiling with no cadence change at all. The claimed mechanism is falsified, twice, on hardware.

3. The residual ("does the honored lifetime stop somewhere between 20 s and 28 s?") is speculation with no supporting measurement, and it is fail-closed AND fully attributable, contrary to the claimed consequence. `_apply_travel_guard` writes `sample["travel_guard_reason"] = "feed_stale"` on the tripping sample (services.py:7639-7650), and the step-response result returns every sample verbatim in `result["samples"]` (services.py:10439). So a lapsed-subscription abort is distinguishable from a distance trip in the same response — only the one-word top-level `reason` summary is coarse, and that coarseness is pre-existing and independent of window length.

No defect demonstrable in the current tree.

Not refuted, but downgraded. The asymmetry is real in the deployed tree: services.py:9690 computes `required = max(max_travel_m + stop_overshoot_m, clock_bound_m)`, where clock_bound_m = 7.5e-04 * linear_speed * window_s carries no stop-overshoot term. The clock branch's own comment (9673-9684) defines it as in-window wall-clock travel, and the mandatory stop is issued after the window ends (travel_abort/stop in the finally at 10411-10430), so the post-stop creep is uncovered on exactly the branch that exists for the guard-no-op mode. The sibling disk helper in the same codebase does include it: continuous_controller.py:551-554 uses `max_safety_speed_mps * max_heading_acquisition_s + stop_overshoot_m`. The branch is reachable at admissible configs (baseline 3000 / step 15000 / settle 5000 = 23000 ms at linear 400, max_travel_m 4.5; step_window_travel_exceeds_budget does not fire since 0.17*23=3.91 <= 4.5) and is pinned by tests/components/mammotion/test_step_response_probe.py:985-1002 asserting required_radius_m == 6.90, i.e. the bare clock bound. The guard's trip conditions (7643-7684) genuinely do not catch a latched x/y with advancing sequence and fresh receipt stamps, so the failure mode the clock branch was written for is the one where the omission bites. The identical omission at 7945-7953 (corridor_must_cover_m) is reporting-only.

However the claimed concrete breach is NOT demonstrable. It assumes real in-window travel equals clock_bound_m (6.90 m). It does not: _PROBE_SPEED_PER_LINEAR_UNIT_MS is rounded up (0.30 vs measured sustained 0.295, +0.115 m over 23 s), takes no ramp credit (the 2026-09-01 run averaged 0.262 m/s whole-window over 15.2 s vs 0.295 sustained, ~0.50 m deficit at 23 s), and `required` is a disk RADIUS compared against path length on a path that must curve (step phase restricted to |angular| in {120,180}). Realistic extent at 23 s / linear 400 is ~6.3 m of path, ~6.75 m including the 0.4544 m creep, still inside 6.90 m. The thinnest case is linear 300 at 23 s (clock bound 5.175 m vs ~4.6 m travel + 0.45 creep = ~5.05 m), roughly 0.12 m of accidental margin. So the defect is a genuine uncertified 0.50 m gap in a safety disk whose actual protection comes from unmodeled ramp/curvature margin the tree elsewhere declines to credit — a real one-line inconsistency, but no reproducible corridor breach. Severity low, not high.
